The pie chart presents the percentage distribution of a fictional arts centre’s annual budget in 2025. It divides the same total allocation into five named areas. These figures describe the composition of that total during one period; they do not provide a sequence of annual measurements or a monetary size for the allocation.

Overall, Performances received the largest share and Publicity the smallest. The two leading areas together accounted for more than half of the total allocation. By contrast, the three other categories together represented less than half, despite covering more named areas.

Performances accounted for 35% of the total, while Workshops represented 22%. The gap between them was 13 percentage points. Their combined share was 57%, compared with 43% for the other three areas taken together.

Among the smaller shares, Equipment stood at 18%, followed by Maintenance at 15%. Publicity made up the remaining 10%, leaving a 25-percentage-point difference between the largest and smallest categories. The percentage figures allow comparisons within this allocation, but they do not establish the absolute amount assigned to any area or explain why those priorities were chosen.
